title: Upper-case the long names without touching the list

blocks.text: A stream pipeline has three parts: a source, zero or more intermediate operations, and exactly one terminal operation that runs the whole thing and produces a result.

Write `LongNames.upperLongNames(List<String> names)`. It returns the names that are **longer than three characters** (every character counts, spaces included), upper-cased with `Locale.ROOT`, in the order they came in; a name that repeats is kept each time. One pipeline fits it well: the list as the source, the filtering and the upper-casing, then a terminal operation that collects the result.
Watch the boundary of "longer than three", and remember whose list you were handed: the caller still owns it after your method returns.

cases.says: It keeps the names longer than three characters, upper-cased, in their order.
A name of exactly three letters is not longer than three, so it is left out.
The list passed in is left exactly as it was: a stream never modifies its source.
The result is a new list, even when every name already qualifies: a later change to the caller's list does not show in it.
Upper-casing uses Locale.ROOT, so "timid" becomes "TIMID" even when the default locale is Turkish.

concepts: A stream never modifies its source, and its operations must not modify the source either.
